{{For|the algebraic topology concept|Relative homology#Definition}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''relative cycle''' is a type of [[algebraic cycle]] on a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]]. In particular, let <math>X</math> be a scheme of finite type over a [[Noetherian scheme]] <math>S</math>, so that <math> X \rightarrow S</math>. Then a relative cycle is a cycle on <math>X</math> which lies over the [[generic point]]s of <math>S</math>, such that the cycle has a well-defined specialization to any [[Fiber (mathematics)#Fiber in algebraic geometry|fiber]] of the projection <math> X \rightarrow S</math>.{{harv|Voevodsky|Suslin|2000}}

The notion was introduced by [[Andrei Suslin]] and [[Vladimir Voevodsky]] in 2000; the authors were motivated to overcome some of the deficiencies of [[sheaves with transfers]].
